note: Player spawn points, from handler-0 records in the decoded level scripts. Handler 0 is the only handler with a field map recovered from its constructor (0x02050C44), and its payload is 12 bytes with the position in the first three s16 fields.

respawn_candidates.hypothesis: Entity id 7 in the arena spawn tables is the respawn point set.
respawn_candidates.why: Reported from play: players respawn all over Jabba, not only the top floor, and probably likewise on Mos. Id 7 fits that shape exactly - 12 records on Jabba spread across FIVE distinct heights (y = 53, 79, 80, 107, 190), including two symmetric groups of four at y=53 and y=107, which is what per-floor respawn points look like. Their 8-byte tails are all zero, so they carry no per-instance configuration, which also suits a plain position marker.
respawn_candidates.confidence: REJECTED - zero landings across 400 teleports in the three-match session
respawn_candidates.how_to_confirm: The RAM recordings already contain player deaths and respawns. Compare a player actor position immediately after a respawn against this list; a match on any of them settles it without a new capture.

confirmation_attempted.method: Searched the frame-indexed trace for actors of the positional player class teleporting more than 25 units between samples, then compared the landing position against both the id-7 candidates and the handler-0 initial spawns.
confirmation_attempted.result: NOT CONFIRMED. Only three teleports occur in the whole recording, and none lands on a candidate or an initial spawn.

the_three.note: single actor - the only plausible respawn, and it matches nothing in either list
both actors jump on the same frame, which is the savestate load the player reported, not a respawn

confirmation_attempted.what_this_means: The evidence is thin rather than contrary - two of the three jumps are a savestate load and the session may simply contain no deaths. But the one candidate respawn does NOT match, so id 7 is weakened and must not be treated as settled.
confirmation_attempted.better_test: Use a recording that definitely contains deaths. The three-match session in out/work/_superseded was recorded with combat and would be the one to re-walk, or watch the HUD heart count in the RAM recording to locate death frames precisely and only then look at positions.

initial_vs_respawn: The handler-0 records are four per arena and read as the INITIAL spawns - the byte at +0x09 runs 0,1,2,3, which is a player index. Id 7 has no such index and is more numerous, which is consistent with a shared respawn pool rather than per-player starts.

CONFIRMED_FROM_RECORDINGS.session: out/work/archive/gpudump_3matches - three matches across Mos Eisley and Jabbas Tower, 6,868 RAM captures.
CONFIRMED_FROM_RECORDINGS.method: Scanned the actor region for position triples that move like an actor - 65 found - then collected every teleport over 30 units and compared the landing position against both spawn lists. 400 teleports checked.

result.handler_0_spawns_CONFIRMED: Landings match them. Jabbas Tower spawn (1,0,-11) was landed on SEVEN times and the Cantina lobby spawn (15,32,-11) three times. Being landed on repeatedly means these points are used for RESPAWNS as well as the initial placement - they are not one-shot starts.
result.id_7_respawn_hypothesis_REJECTED: Zero of the 400 teleports landed on any of the 15 id-7 candidates, across both maps. The distribution argument - 12 points over five floors with zero tails - was suggestive and wrong.

CONFIRMED_FROM_RECORDINGS.so_what_is_id_7: Unknown again. It is NOT the respawn set and NOT a grapple. Both readings are now recorded as failed.
CONFIRMED_FROM_RECORDINGS.open_question: The player reports respawning in many places across Jabbas Tower, but the only confirmed landings are the four handler-0 points. Either respawn positions are computed at runtime rather than placed - picked from nav data or from a spawn nearest the death, which would leave no table to find - or a further set exists that this scan missed. The scan only inspected 400 of 1,163 teleports, so widening it is the cheap next step before concluding anything.
